About this program
Curriculum and Instruction, Doctor of Philosophy
Advance your expertise in curriculum and instruction through a research-intensive PhD that prepares you to improve teaching, learning, and curriculum through research and leadership.
Explore, research, and shape how students learn
The Curriculum and Instruction PhD prepares experienced educators and professionals to become scholars, researchers, and leaders in teaching, learning, and curriculum design. Through advanced coursework, seminars, and close collaboration with faculty, you'll explore the theories, research, and ideas that shape curriculum and instruction while examining how they influence educational practice.
As you develop expertise in your area of interest, you'll build advanced skills in quantitative and qualitative research and learn to connect scholarship with questions that matter in education. The program culminates in an original dissertation that contributes new knowledge to the field. Graduates are prepared to advance curriculum and instruction through research, publication, university teaching, educational leadership, and other roles that shape how and what students learn.
Build a PhD around your interests
Drawing on faculty expertise across three College of Education units, this research-intensive PhD gives you access to a broad range of perspectives in curriculum, teaching, learning, and educational research. Rather than following a one-size-fits-all path, you'll work closely with a faculty advisor to design a program of study aligned with your academic and professional goals.
You'll complete 15 units of discipline-specific coursework in a focus area such as teacher education, early childhood education, elementary education, literacy, or educational technology. Small doctoral seminars provide opportunities to engage closely with faculty and peers while developing your scholarly interests. Based on the Flagstaff campus with online and blended coursework, the program combines meaningful faculty mentorship with flexibility for working professionals.
Turn your expertise into educational impact
Graduates are prepared to shape teaching, learning, and curriculum through careers in higher education, preK-12 education, government, and other education-focused organizations. Many pursue faculty and research positions, teaching future educators while contributing new knowledge in areas such as curriculum and instruction, teacher education, literacy, early childhood education, and educational technology. Others lead curriculum development and evaluation, instructional design, educational technology, or school and district improvement initiatives. Whether you pursue scholarship, teaching, or educational leadership, you'll be prepared to apply your expertise to strengthen curriculum, inform educational practice, and influence how students learn.
Develop your voice as an education researcher
Research is central to the Curriculum and Instruction PhD experience. You'll build a strong foundation in quantitative and qualitative approaches through 12 units of research methods coursework, with opportunities to pursue additional methods aligned with your research interests. Working closely with faculty mentors, you'll learn to evaluate existing scholarship, develop theoretical frameworks, design studies, analyze findings, and connect research to meaningful questions in teaching, learning, and curriculum.
As your skills develop, you'll gain experience communicating research to professional and public audiences and preparing scholarly work for publication. Your doctoral experience culminates in an original, faculty-guided dissertation that allows you to investigate a topic of personal and professional significance and contribute new knowledge to the field.
Graduate contact
Contact CandIDocProgram@nau.edu to learn more about the Curriculum and Instruction PhD. We encourage prospective students to connect with the program coordinator before applying.
